newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says will ensure French army gets resources.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says will ensure French army gets resources.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Sunday he would make sure that the armed forces, anxious at possible budget cuts by the new left-wing government, received the resources they needed.

The conservative president told a Defence Ministry reception on the eve of the Bastille Day military parade: "As head of the armed forces, I will take care that our forces continue to have the necessary resources both for their renovation and to maintain their capabilities and their training."

Chirac, who launched a major shift from conscription to all-professional armed forces last year, said he would review with the Socialist-led government what objectives had been met after the first year of a 1996 six-year military planning law.

Under the constitution, the president is commander-in-chief but has no control over the defence budget, which is adopted by the government and enacted by parliament. The centre-right government defeated in last month's parliamentary election had pledged to hold defence spending level for five years.
Senior army officers were worried by the appointment of a tough budget expert, Socialist Alain Richard, with no military expertise, as defence minister last month.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has not yet set 1998 spending targets for the defence ministry, although he has sent written instructions to all other ministers, fuelling speculation that he may seek substantial cuts, perhaps by delaying or scrapping costly weapons programmes.
